n: After three days of fasting, Esther puts on her royal robes and stands in the inner court, in full view of the king on his throne. Her fast prepared her spirit; her robes prepared her for the task.

f.g: Literally “put on royalty” — she clothed herself in her queenly role.

n: The king is pleased to see her and holds out the golden scepter. Esther touches its tip — her life is spared. The prayers of her people are answered.

f.w: she obtained favour in his sight
touched the top of the sceptre
f.g: A gesture accepting the king’s mercy and permission to speak.

n: The king realizes she must want something important and offers up to half his kingdom — a royal figure of speech for great generosity.

f.w: to the half of the kingdom

n: Instead of making her request immediately, Esther wisely invites the king and Haman to a banquet. She chooses her moment carefully.

f.w: If it seem good unto the king

n: The king has Haman summoned quickly, and both come to Esther’s feast.
Over wine, the king again asks what she wants, repeating his promise of up to half the kingdom.

f.g: The wine-drinking part of the feast, after the meal.

n: Esther begins to answer — and then pauses. The suspense builds.

f.w: My petition and my request is
f.g: She begins, then holds back her real request.

n: She asks them to return for a second banquet the next day, when she will reveal her request. Her patience creates time — and during that night, God will turn events in a surprising way.
Haman leaves overjoyed — until he sees Mordecai at the gate, who neither stands nor trembles before him. His joy instantly turns to fury.

f.g: Did not even flinch or show fear.

n: Haman controls himself in public, then goes home and gathers his friends and his wife, Zeresh.
He boasts about his wealth, his many sons, and his promotions. Pride is fully on display.
He brags that he alone was invited with the king to the queen’s banquet — not knowing that the queen is a Jew and that the invitation is a trap.

f.g: Ironic — he thinks it is an honor, but it will be his downfall.

n: Yet all this means nothing to him while Mordecai sits at the gate. One wounded pride outweighs all his blessings — a portrait of how envy and hatred steal joy.

f.w: so long as I see Mordecai

n: His wife and friends suggest building an enormous gallows — about 75 feet tall — and asking the king the next morning to execute Mordecai on it. Haman likes the idea and has it built at once.

f.g: Probably a tall pole or stake for impaling or displaying a body.
About 75 feet (23 meters) — designed to be seen across the city.
